_comment: THE PRIVACY CONTRACT. This is the ONLY hand-edited definition of what may leave the machine.
scripts/gen_contract.py emits, all committed, all `git diff --exit-code`'d in CI:
Packages/BuilderKit/Sources/BuilderSync/Generated/UploadContract.swift
server/builder/contract.py            (Pydantic, extra='forbid')
mobile/src/generated/contract.ts
web/public/upload-fields.json         (publicly served; what the verification curl fetches)
PRIVACY.md                            (the prose claim, from the same source)
THE STRUCTURAL GUARANTEE IS THE SERIALIZER, NOT THE TEST.
SessionUpload implements encode(to:) by hand as
var c = encoder.container(keyedBy: UploadField.self)
There is NO synthesized Codable and NO hand-written CodingKeys struct anywhere in BuilderSync.
A field absent from the generated UploadField enum is UNREPRESENTABLE ON THE WIRE. Adding a
stored property to any model therefore cannot change the payload. Deleting a line from this
file deletes a field from the product.
NOT PRESENT, AND NOT ADDABLE WITHOUT EDITING THIS FILE:
prompt text, assistant text, thinking blocks, tool inputs, tool outputs, file contents,
diffs, structuredPatch, file paths, file NAMES, directory names, commit MESSAGES,
commit SHAs, BRANCH NAMES, cwd, git origin URL, repo names for anonymous repos,
MCP server names, terminal commands or output, environment variables, URLs fetched,
hostname, IP address.
THE ONE DELIBERATE EXCEPTION (v2): `analysis`. It is model-written prose about the session,
produced on the user's own machine by their own Claude Code from a digest of the transcript,
and its shape is fixed by spec/analysis.v1.json (every string bounded, extra keys rejected).
It may name files and features in prose, and `decision_patterns[].prompt_excerpt` carries
SHORT VERBATIM PROMPT QUOTES, capped at 160 characters each. It is OPT-IN, nullable, omitted
from the wire when off, private to the account under RLS, and leaves the account only when
the session is explicitly shared. Everything else on the list above still holds: no field
outside `analysis` carries prose, and `analysis` itself carries no paths, diffs, tool I/O,
commit messages, branch names, URLs, hostnames or raw prompts.
THE SECOND FIELD ADDED SINCE v2 (v3): `feedback`. What ONE sitting cost you, for the card you
read once and close: a stretch that went nowhere, a run of failures, a file rewritten over and
over. It is NOT a second `analysis` and needed no exception, because it carries no prose at all
— an id from a fixed list of three, and two integers. The SENTENCE is written on the phone from
that id, so nothing about the wording travels either.
What it deliberately does NOT carry, and both were in the local version of these notes:
* the FAILING COMMAND. `analysis/feedback.py` says "4 failures in a row on `bun test`" on your
own machine. Terminal commands are on the never-list above and stay there; the wire says how
many and for how long.
* the FILE NAME. The local note names the file that was rewritten five times. `analysis` may
name files in prose because it is opt-in and bounded; this field is neither, so it says
"a file" and the name stays on the machine.
Two design contradictions resolved here, deliberately:
1. Branch names are DELETED ENTIRELY. One design's never-list banned them while another
uploaded them for public repos. Branch was read by zero cards and zero queries, so
deleting it makes both documents true at zero product cost. 'feat/acquisition-flow'
leaks roadmap more reliably than a repo name does.
2. NO PROMPT OR FILE NAME LEAVES IN ANY MODE. Three designs built a server titling
endpoint carrying first_prompt/last_prompt/commit_messages/file_basenames. It is
deleted, not restricted — every harness already writes a title to disk. This is also
what makes the falsification command on /privacy safe to publish.
_excluded_note: visibility 'excluded' is not a mode: an excluded repo produces ZERO uploads, and if ANY event in a session resolves to an excluded repo the ENTIRE session is dropped — never partially uploaded, never uploaded under the primary repo's visibility.

fields.name: client_session_id
fields.doc: stable opaque session id; also the Idempotency-Key

fields.name: machine_id
fields.doc: sha256 of this Mac's platform UUID

fields.name: content_hash
fields.doc: hash of this payload; lets sync skip unchanged sessions

fields.name: client_version
fields.doc: agent version

fields.name: sessionizer_version
fields.doc: so a retuned boundary is a recompute, not a migration

fields.name: active_calc_version
fields.doc: so a retuned active-time formula is a recompute

fields.name: agent_observed_at
fields.doc: when the agent produced this payload: the finalize instant for final, the snapshot instant for live

fields.name: client_clock_offset_ms
fields.doc: measured against the server Date header

fields.name: active_seconds
fields.doc: union of turn spans and capped gaps; the honest headline

fields.name: state
fields.doc: live = an open/idle session snapshot, replaced in place when it finalizes; final = complete

fields.name: end_reason
fields.doc: why the session ended (docs/session-boundaries.md). still_running IS the live upload; cleared (a typed /clear) and switched_repo (a new session opened in another repo) are v3 ends that, like idle_gap, mean the work stopped

fields.name: attended_seconds
fields.doc: active time with a human evidently present (docs/session-boundaries.md)

fields.name: autonomous_seconds
fields.doc: active time after the human went quiet for > tauAutonomousSec

fields.name: presence_count
fields.doc: typed prompts + interrupts + human file edits

fields.name: unattended
fields.doc: zero presence signals. Hours only: no record, no streak, no notification

fields.name: visible
fields.doc: counts toward hours, graph, streaks

fields.name: notable
fields.doc: eligible for a card or a record

fields.name: strip_columns
fields.doc: 1024 bytes: 2-bit class, 2-bit density. No text, no paths, by construction

fields.name: strip_marks
fields.doc: [{ms, k}] where k is prompt|commit|compact

fields.name: prompt_count_basis
fields.doc: so Cursor's looser rule never sums with Claude Code's

fields.name: tool_calls
fields.doc: allowlisted tool names only; unknown and MCP names bucket to mcp_other / other

fields.name: lines_added_agent
fields.doc: live-path only; rewound edits never landed

fields.name: human_edit_events
fields.doc: count of edited_text_file / humanChanges signals. Existence only — these carry no line counts

fields.name: agent_line_bucket
fields.doc: a 5-way LOWER BOUND, never a percentage

fields.name: tokens_reported
fields.doc: false for EVERY Cursor session, forever — Cursor never writes token counts locally

fields.name: tokens
fields.doc: five separate buckets. Null, never zero, when unreported

fields.name: abandoned_branch_tokens
fields.doc: tokens spent on rewound DAG branches. You paid for them

fields.name: token_dedupe
fields.doc: server rejects none + tokens_reported: that is the 1.88x arriving unlabeled

fields.name: token_scope
fields.doc: 'flat' is NOT a legal value — it would let the ~3x subagent glob overcount in wearing a legitimate label

fields.name: models
fields.doc: [{model_id, output_token_share}] — labels only. The [1m] suffix is preserved verbatim

fields.name: model_state
fields.doc: Cursor is ~84% unknown: modelName is 'default' on 115 of 137 composers

fields.name: repo_hash
fields.doc: HMAC of the normalized origin URL. Full 64 hex, never truncated

fields.name: repo_name
fields.doc: PUBLIC REPOS ONLY. Absent from the anonymous key set entirely

fields.name: title
fields.doc: PUBLIC REPOS ONLY. The title the HARNESS already wrote to your disk. Never model-generated by us

fields.name: card_png_url
fields.doc: populated ONLY when you tap Share. The image you chose to publish; contains no field not listed above

fields.name: analysis
fields.doc: model-written reading of the session, produced on the user's machine by their own Claude Code from a digest of the transcript (spec/analysis.v1.json). Present only when analysis upload is enabled. Private to the account under RLS; leaves it only when the session is shared. This is the ONE field that carries prose derived from prompts and code, and it is opt-in for exactly that reason.

fields.name: feedback
fields.doc: what this one sitting cost that you would not have chosen: [{id, seconds, count}] where id is one of three fixed notes. Numbers only — no command, no file name, no prose. Computed on the machine (analysis/feedback.py); the sentence is rendered on the phone. Null, never [], when the sitting had nothing worth saying
